table.title: [val][adversarial] Long group header over tiny sub-columns
table.html:
ModelBenchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suites (%)Notes

Base797570Default

understanding.purpose: Compare benchmark accuracy across three language evaluations for each model, alongside explanatory notes.
understanding.reading: Readers scan down each language column to compare models and across each row to compare a model’s scores and note. Wrapped notes can increase row height, which can also accommodate wrapping elsewhere in the row.
groups: EN, ZH, and AR are parallel accuracy measures under one shared benchmark heading and should have equal widths.
Model identifies each row; Notes supplies context for that row.
keep_intact: Language identifiers EN, ZH, and AR
Words within the benchmark heading and notes
may_wrap: The shared benchmark heading can wrap across multiple lines over the three language columns.
Notes can wrap naturally at word boundaries.

preferred.name: r2A
preferred.note: Give the language columns a little more space than r1A while retaining most of its Notes width; test whether the heading or notes wrap more favorably near this boundary.

preferred.name: r3B
preferred.note: Stay close to r2A’s more comfortable note measure, with a modest increase to the score group to test whether the heading wraps more efficiently.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Reclaim the unused Model width from r0C and distribute it between the score group and Notes. This tests whether a slightly wider shared heading can improve its wrapping without making notes excessively narrow.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Give the shared benchmark heading more room than in r0C while retaining more space for Notes than r0B. This explores a middle ground between header compactness and note readability.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Refine r1C by returning 3px to Notes while keeping the language group close to the width that shortened the shared heading.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Test a slightly wider shared heading to see whether it gains a better line break without making the notes substantially taller.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Test a midpoint between r2A and r2B: give the shared heading more room than r2A while returning 6px to Notes compared with r2B.

acceptable.name: r3C
acceptable.note: Explore a wider shared heading to see whether it gains a useful line break; the narrower Notes column makes this a deliberate comparison of header and body rhythm.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: The numeric columns receive far more room than their two-character values need, leaving only 53px of text width for Notes. That is narrower than its longest word and would force word splits and excessive wrapping.
bad.why: The numeric columns receive far more room than their two-character values need, leaving only 53px of text width for Notes. That is narrower than its longest word and would force word splits and excessive wrapping.

rationale: r2A and r3B give the three comparable accuracy columns equal widths while reserving enough space for the prose in Notes. Their group header takes six lines, but the longer note reads in five lines, preserving a useful balance between the header and body. The alternatives with wider accuracy columns shorten the group header but make the longest note more fragmented; r3C takes that tradeoff furthest.

general: Give columns with the same role a consistent width when their contents have similar needs.
Judge width by the whole table: a merged heading and body prose can compete for space even when individual data values are short.
Keep words intact and assess the rhythm of wrapped text, not just total table height.
specific: The three accuracy columns contain short labels and values, so they can remain narrow without harming comparison.
A few extra pixels in Notes let the longest note use five lines in r2A and r3B, while the group heading remains legible.

tradeoffs: r1C, r2B and r2C give the group heading a shorter five-line wrap at the cost of a six-line note. r3C gives the heading the same benefit but narrows Notes further, producing a seven-line note.
uncertain: A designer who gives the group heading more weight could reasonably prefer r2B or r2C. The ranges describe the observed preferred variants, not a tested guarantee for every intermediate width; the three accuracy widths should change together, with Notes taking the remaining space.

critique.good: The notes have enough width for relatively natural phrases, and the model names and scores remain intact. The three score columns have equal widths.
critique.problems: ZH breaks across two lines, weakening the parallel language headers. The shared benchmark heading is tall, leaving a large blank area in the adjacent headers.
critique.cause: Each 42px score column leaves 21px for text, 1px less than ZH needs. Their combined width also forces the shared heading into six lines.

critique.good: All language identifiers stay intact, and the wider score group gives the shared heading a more compact shape. Model names remain intact.
critique.problems: The notes are cramped into short phrases, especially for Small and Large. The resulting tall rows make it harder to scan and compare scores.
critique.cause: The 59px score columns take space from Notes, leaving it only 95px of text width.

critique.good: All identifiers and scores stay intact. Notes have a more comfortable measure than in r0B, and the score columns remain equal.
critique.problems: The shared heading is still six lines tall, while the Small note wraps into six lines. The extra space in Model does little to improve readability.
critique.cause: The 76px Model column exceeds the 66px needed to fit its longest word. The three 45px score columns leave the group heading narrow, and Notes receives 148px.

critique.good: The equal language columns make the three scores easy to compare, and the generous Notes column gives the longer note a reasonably natural line length. Model names, scores, and words remain intact.
critique.problems: The shared benchmark heading forms a tall, narrow block that dominates the top of the table. The language columns feel cramped, although their values fit.
critique.cause: At 43px each, the three language columns give the spanning heading only 129px in total. The 164px Notes column takes much of the available width.

critique.good: The equal language columns give the scores slightly more breathing room, and the Large-model note reads comfortably across three lines.
critique.problems: The shared heading remains six lines tall, while the Small-model note grows to six lines. That makes the table taller without a clear visual gain over r1A.
critique.cause: Increasing each language column to 47px leaves 152px for Notes, which crosses a wrapping threshold for the Small-model note without shortening the heading.

critique.good: The wider group makes the benchmark heading shorter and gives the three measures a more open rhythm. The equal score columns remain easy to scan.
critique.problems: The Notes column is visibly narrow: both longer notes break into short phrases, and the Small-model row remains tall. The extra space around the tiny scores comes at the expense of the explanatory text.
critique.cause: The 51px language columns leave 140px for Notes, or 119px of text width after padding and borders.

critique.good: The model names, language identifiers, scores and note words remain intact. The wider Notes column gives the longer note a relatively comfortable measure, and the three score columns read as a matched group.
critique.problems: The benchmark heading forms a tall, narrow block, leaving a large empty area under Notes and delaying the data. The score columns are also visually cramped.
critique.cause: At 45px each, the three score columns give the shared heading only 135px across, while Notes receives 158px.

critique.good: The wider score group makes the shared heading shorter and gives EN, ZH and AR a more even, readable rhythm. Model names and values remain intact.
critique.problems: The first note becomes taller and more fragmented, largely offsetting the reduction in header height. The Notes column looks tight beside the expanded score group.
critique.cause: Increasing each score column to 50px reduces Notes to 143px, causing the first note to wrap onto an extra line.

critique.good: The benchmark heading remains relatively compact, and the equal score columns clearly communicate three parallel measures. All identifiers and values remain intact.
critique.problems: The extra space in the score columns produces little visible benefit over r2B, while Notes becomes more constrained. The long first note still creates a tall row.
critique.cause: The 52px score columns leave only 137px for Notes; the additional 6px allocated to the score group does not shorten the heading or table.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

ref_equal.why: The narrow Notes column breaks words across lines and makes the data rows extremely tall, while the numeric columns have more space than they need.

ref_auto.why: Notes remain readable and the three numeric columns are balanced. The group heading wraps to five lines, but its hierarchy stays clear.

r1B.why: The compact numeric columns leave useful space for Notes, and words stay intact. The six-line group heading is tall relative to its subcolumns.

r2A.why: The numeric columns are compact and evenly sized, giving Notes enough room to read comfortably. The group heading takes six lines.

r1C.why: The group heading fits in five lines, the language columns are balanced, and Notes wraps without splitting words. The first data row is still fairly tall.

contrast.why: Notes is so narrow that words split across lines and rows become very tall. The Model and numeric columns occupy space that would be more useful in Notes.

raw.unsure: B, D and E are close: D gives Notes the most comfortable line lengths, while B and E give the group heading a shorter wrap.

r2A.why: The model names and scores scan clearly, and the notes have useful space. The grouped header is quite tall, but its words remain intact.

contrast.why: The notes column is so narrow that words split across lines, making the notes hard to read and stretching the rows excessively.

r1C.why: The score columns are balanced and the notes remain readable. The group header breaks held-out across lines and leaves its percentage marker on a line by itself.

r1B.why: The notes read comfortably, model names fit, and the similar score columns are easy to compare. The grouped header is tall but keeps its words intact.

ref_auto.why: The score columns and notes are readable, with a clear grouping of the three languages. The grouped header splits held-out and leaves the percentage marker alone.

ref_equal.why: The wide score columns leave too little room for notes, breaking words and creating very tall rows with large empty areas.

raw.unsure: A is a close alternative; the small differences in score-column widths and note wrapping make the preference for D marginal.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
